title: ECAT agent output (e-category-rater) -- ONE GROUP of similar questions, 1 run
description: ITEM GRANULARITY: the item is a GROUP of up to six questions sharing a subject and an E1 question type, not one question. That is deliberate and is the correction for v1's central defect -- v1 was tagged in paper order, and so gave one match-list question `check_each_statement` and another `elimination` with no stated reason for the difference. Rule 0.7 of docs/question_categories/RULEBOOK.md requires similar questions to be judged against each other, which is only possible if the agent sees them together. Hence `ratings` is an array and `group_note` is required: the note is where the agent records how the group was kept consistent and why any member differs, which is the thing v1 had no way to say. Packets are built by scripts/build_ecat_packets.py (580 questions -> 45 subject x type groups -> 120 packets). Every enum here is config/allowed_values.yaml v0.3, generated from the rulebook by scripts/build_allowed_values.py, so a label the rulebook defines is emittable and one it retired is not.

group.description: Copied verbatim from the input's `group`. Checked, because a mismatch means the output was written against a different packet.

question_id.description: Must be one of the question_ids the packet supplied, and each supplied id must appear exactly once. Enforced in scripts/checks/ECAT.py: a group judged 'together' that silently drops a member has not been judged together. TWO ID SHAPES ARE VALID: `Q-000123` for the v1 sheet, and `2015_A#q041` for the papers_v2 corpus, whose packets are built by scripts/build_ecat_packets_v2.py. The v2 ids are NOT translated into Q-ids: a synthetic id in the v1 shape would join wrongly to the v1 sheet, and the two corpora are reported separately on purpose.

concept.description: The specific thing tested, in a form a student could revise: 'Critical angle from relative speeds', not 'formula_or_law'. The rulebook's section 3 calls this the single most useful field on the sheet, because a student cannot revise a broad content_shape. May be "" only as the stated unsure form, with the reason in `note`.

cognitive_demand.description: config/allowed_values.yaml `cognitive_demand`, v0.3 (rulebook section 4a), plus "" as the unsure form. `new_demand` is the escape hatch and REQUIRES a description in `note` -- it is the correct answer when none of the eight fits, and using it is how the vocabulary gets revised instead of quietly stretched. Note that `application` no longer means 'a student who memorised nothing can still reach the answer' -- that v1 definition was untenable, since applying a rule requires knowing the rule.

solution_structure.description: config/allowed_values.yaml `solution_structure`, v0.3 (rulebook section 4b), plus "" as the unsure form. FOUR INDEPENDENT MATCH-CHECKS ARE NOT FOUR DEPENDENT STEPS: `multi_step_dependent` requires step 2 to need step 1's RESULT. This is the distinction v1's single `multi_step` label could not express.

strategy_available.description: Zero or more, from config/allowed_values.yaml `strategy_available`, v0.3 (rulebook section 4c). A recall question CAN offer elimination -- that is no longer a contradiction, because recall is a demand and elimination a strategy, which v1 had on one axis as siblings.

strategy_evidence.description: REQUIRED (non-empty) when `strategy_available` contains `elimination`: name the one pair or fact and the options it strikes out -- 'fibrous -> skull bones appears only in option 2'. Enforced in scripts/checks/ECAT.py. No evidence, no label.

traps.description: One entry per wrong option that carries a device. MAY BE EMPTY, and MUST be empty when `review_status` is `source_incomplete` -- rulebook rule 5. A trap inferred from a question whose figure or option is missing is a guess dressed as a finding, and scripts/checks/ECAT.py fails it.

label.description: config/allowed_values.yaml `trap`, v0.3 -- 37 values, generated from rulebook section 5. The enum is NOT repeated here: scripts/checks/ECAT.py reads allowed_values.yaml directly, so the trap list cannot drift between the rulebook, the config and this schema the way it did between v0.2 and v1.

option.description: The ONE option this device lands on. Must not be the official answer: there is no trap on the answer.

route.description: The mistake that leads there -- 'uses 1/2 LI instead of 1/2 LI^2'. Rulebook rule 4: a trap tag that cannot name the option and the route is not actionable and must be omitted instead.

verdicts.description: config/allowed_values.yaml `trap_verdict`, v0.3 (rulebook section 5a). These are NOT traps and are kept in a separate field so they cannot be counted as examiner design. `source_damage_artifact` is our own extraction damage and was the commonest device the per-subject analyses recorded; `arguable_key` is a review flag and never overturns the printed key.

reason.description: The rulebook's fixed shape: 'This question requires ___, demonstrated by ___.' The second blank QUOTES the stem or an option. A reason about students is not a reason -- we hold no response data, so 'a common error' and 'no student would pick this' are unsupportable (SPEC Rule 22). scripts/checks/ECAT.py rejects those phrasings.

note.description: Universal rule 7, and where the unsure forms put their reason. Optional.

question_type.description: E1 -- the shape on the page, decided FROM LAYOUT ALONE: nothing about difficulty or method. Added 2026-10-21 for the papers_v2 corpus. In v1 this was filled by the separate E1 step, so ECAT had no field for it and a rater working this corpus could only record its reading in prose -- which is a label the product cannot show. `new_type` is the escape for a shape the list does not cover; name what you saw in `reason`.

secondary_type.description: E1's second shape, where a question genuinely has two. Optional.

format.description: E2 -- what the ANSWER must contain, decided FROM THE OPTIONS ALONE and never from how the answer is obtained. A question that involves a ratio can still ask for a temperature. `new_format` is the escape.

content_shape.description: E3 -- the broad kind of NCERT material the question is built on. Paired with `concept`, which names the actual concept: the broad label alone is not revisable. `new_shape` is the escape.

group_note.description: How the group was kept consistent, and why any member differs: 'All four are recall of tabulated associations; Q-000052 differs in having a one-pair shortcut, which is why it alone carries elimination.' REQUIRED, because this field is the whole reason the item is a group. An empty note means the questions were judged one at a time, which is the v1 failure this step exists to prevent.

oneOf.description: Universal rule 8: if the input file is missing or broken, the agent writes only {"error": "..."}.
